D.t: Ned Lamont leads by 18.4 in the forecast and wins 100% of simulations. The cushion is about 264,283 votes; a one point swing is about 7,178 voters changing sides.
In 8 of 10 simulations the result lands between D +10.8 and D +25.9. Only an unusual polling error changes the winner.
The polls page average is D +19.2. Your best recent poll is Sacred Heart University / WFSB / CT Insider at D +25.7; your worst is co/efficient (R) at D +10.8. 6 polls in the last 30 days.

The biggest vote banks for Democrats: Hartford, a projected net 115,099 votes; Fairfield, a projected net 88,915 votes; New Haven, a projected net 40,553 votes. Every point of extra turnout here is worth more than persuasion anywhere else.
The large counties within 12 points: New London, D +11.5, 8.9% of the vote; Tolland, D +5.0, 5.3% of the vote; Litchfield, R +5.2, 4.9% of the vote.

D.h: Where you run behind the 2024 map
D.t: Against the 2024 presidential vote, Ned Lamont runs furthest behind in Tolland, Windham, New London. That is where the forecast sees voters who backed your side two years ago and have not come back yet.

Groups big enough to move the race: White voters, 79% of voters, 55 to 44, where a 5 point gain is worth 3.96 points; Large counties, 72% of voters, 61 to 37, where a 5 point gain is worth 3.58 points; Voters who cast ballots in 2022 and 2024, 64% of voters, 60 to 39, where a 5 point gain is worth 3.19 points.
The forecast's worst groups for Ned Lamont: Immigration voters 24 to 75, Incomes $125K and up 51 to 48, Midsize counties 52 to 47. Cutting the loss here is often cheaper than winning new groups.
